description: All three options set at the instance to NON-default values simultaneously (ALWAYS, any-failure, throw), so each is individually observable and each is wrong if a port silently substitutes a default. instanceLocale is ru and fallbackLocale is en, giving a two-candidate walk. Three keys serve different purposes. 'Items.Sparse {{tag}}' under-declares Russian's categories so itemCount 5 fails at ru with RESOLUTION_FAILURE, and its en counterpart interpolates the caller-supplied tag so the bidi setting shows in a resolved translation. 'Sparse.RuOnly {{tag}}' fails the same way at ru but has NO en counterpart, so the walk ends in a failure whose attemptedLocales separates the inherited any-failure ([ru, en]) from the library default ([ru]) — without this key an inherited policy is invisible, because on a plain MISSING_TRANSLATION any-failure and the default behave identically. 'Absent.Named {{tag}}' is in no catalog at all, driving the options through interpolateFailureKey where isolation keys off the LOOKUP locale. Every key carries a placeholder so bidi stays observable even when the handler responds.

Items.Sparse {{tag}}.commentary: Only ONE and OTHER declared. itemCount 5 selects Russian MANY, which is missing, so getInternal throws and getResult classifies the attempt as RESOLUTION_FAILURE. An en counterpart exists, so a permissive policy resolves.

Sparse.RuOnly {{tag}}.commentary: Same sparse declaration, but deliberately ABSENT from en. A RESOLUTION_FAILURE at ru followed by a missing en entry is the only shape in which an inherited any-failure policy is observable through attemptedLocales while the handler still responds.
